messages:
maria_infra: Heads-up — scheduled maintenance for AZ6 tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. Purpose: powercap tuning and soft node drains after an unexpected thermal spike last week. Affects GPU pools: gradient-pool-az6 and dedicated-az6-small. Expect transient capacity reduction (~15%) while we cycle cohorts. @priya_oncall @jin_sre :warning:
jin_sre: Ack. Can you paste the cohort list and backfill plan?
maria_infra: Cohorts are cohort-a (20 nodes), cohort-b (25 nodes). Plan: staggered soft drains (5 nodes at a time), verify KV-cache warmup before allowing new allocations, then do rolling powercap adjustments. Backfill from eu-nearby and us-east1 spot for non-SLA workloads.
alex_runtime: Recommend enabling aggressive prefix cache for the duration to reduce cold-token load. I'll push a temporary batching tweak: max_batch_ms -> 8ms for these pools.
priya_oncall: I'll take oncall for the window. If errors spike >5% for 10m we abort and rollback powercap. Add rollback playbook link?
maria_infra: Rollback playbook: https://confluence.redwood/infra/az6-powercap-rollback (added to runbook). Playbook steps include: revert powercap, uncordon nodes, increase warmup timeout to 90s, notify customers.
sam_prod: Heads-up from product — can we minimize impact to Dedicated customers? If we need to failover requests, prefer model-variant fallback rather than rejecting. Also notify accounts with active Dedicated capacity.
alex_runtime: We'll set routing policy: prefer same-region fallback -> if not available, route to model-variant-latency-optimized. Config snippet: ```policy: - prefer_region: az6 - fallback: variant:latopt - max_tokens_delta: 0.2```
jin_sre: Ops checklist snapshot:
- create maintenance k8s label: `maintenance=az6-2025-01`
- cordon nodes with `kubectl cordon node-<id>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (soft drain script will sleep 30s between pods)
- monitor `gpu_temp` and `nvlink_err` metrics
- capacity watch: AWS ASG warmup 10m
I'll paste the exact commands into the runbook before EOD.
maria_infra: We'll run a canary on cohort-a first (5 nodes). If canary passes 30m of latency/error checks we continue. Expected customer-visible latency bump: ~10-30ms for affected requests during warmup.
priya_oncall: Notifying customers: draft sent to sales+cs for Dedicated accounts in AZ6, asking them to expect potential brief degradation and fallback to variant. @sam_prod please review.
sam_prod: Reviewed. Small wording change then OK. Send at T-6h.
deploy-bot: Calendar event created: "AZ6 powercap tuning & soft drain" 2025-01-22T02:00:00Z -> 2025-01-22T04:00:00Z. Organizer: maria_infra.
jin_sre: Cost note: using eu-nearby and us-east1 spot for backfill may add transient egress + spot allocation overhead (~$1.5k estimated for the window). If we instead use reserved warm spare in az6 it would be ~ $3.8k/month pro-rated. Flagging for finance visibility.
maria_infra: Thanks. We'll proceed with spot backfill and add a hard cap in the orchestration to avoid runaway egress. I'll post the final runbook link once updated. :thumbsup:
priya_oncall: One more: add a synthetic that hammer-tests the model-variant fallback path during canary so we validate routing.
alex_runtime: Done — synthetic id: synth-az6-fallback-01. Results will be in the console dashboard.
maria_infra: Great. See you in the channel during the window. If anything looks off we abort and uncordon. :wave:
